- `AbstractValidator.IValidator.ValidateAsync` is the matching async implementation, at `AbstractValidator.cs:90`.

- `ConditionBuilder.When` is at `Internal/ConditionBuilder.cs:50`, inside its local `Condition` function.

- `ConditionBuilder.UnlessAsync` calls `ConditionBuilder.WhenAsync`.
- `AbstractValidator.When` (the context overload) calls `ConditionBuilder.When`.
- `AbstractValidator.Unless` (the context overload) calls `ConditionBuilder.Unless`.
- `AbstractValidator.WhenAsync` (the context overload) calls `ConditionBuilder.WhenAsync`.

- The single-argument `AbstractValidator.When`, `Unless`, `WhenAsync` and `UnlessAsync` overloads wrap their predicate and forward to the context overloads. They reach it one level further up.
- `DefaultValidatorOptions.Unless` and `UnlessAsync` delegate to `When` and `WhenAsync`. I did not open these bodies, so I'm inferring that from their signatures and the method names.
- `DefaultValidatorExtensions.ChildRules` is at `DefaultValidatorExtensions.cs:1178`. Its display-name lambda calls `GetDisplayName` on a rule, which can end up in `RuleBase.IValidationRule.GetDisplayName`.
- `ValidatorDescriptor.GetName` calls `GetDisplayName(null)`, so it only reaches the function if that call passes a non-null context. Its callers go through the same interface.

**Test files that exercise it**
- `src/FluentValidation.Tests/ConditionTests.cs` uses the `When((_, c) => …)` context overloads at lines 259, 275, 293, 312 and 318. These go through `DefaultValidatorOptions.When`.
- `src/FluentValidation.Tests/AbstractValidatorTester.cs` casts the validator to `IValidator` at lines 203–215. I haven't confirmed that those tests call `Validate(IValidationContext)`, so this entry is the weakest.
- `src/FluentValidation.Tests/RuleBuilderTests.cs` calls `rule.GetDisplayName(null)` at lines 56, 126, 135 and 159. With a null context, `RuleBase` doesn't call `GetFromNonGenericContext`, so these tests don't actually reach it.

In `SharedConditionTests.cs`, the `(x, c)` lambdas on `WhenAsync` bind to the `(T, CancellationToken)` overload, not the context one.
